description: Sky similarity search: find the past or future dates whose planetary positions best match a reference sky, ranked by a stated angular distance in degrees. E.g. {reference: '2026-10-29T00:00Z', direction: 'past', bodies: ['jupiter', 'saturn']}. Searches a date grid (1 hour to 1 week steps, 1800-2200) for the skies closest to a reference: by longitude, by the separations between bodies, by declination, optionally with the same retrograde flags. The score is a weighted mean angular distance in degrees, defined in result.settings.metric. Data for your own analysis — never a signal or forecast. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.25 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/astronomy/sky-analogues (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

bodies.description: Bodies to match. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

direction.description: Search before the reference (with a local date-time and place: before that moment), after it, or both (default; the only choice with reference.values without 'datetime').

features.description: What to compare: 'longitude' (default), 'separations' (the angle between every pair of bodies), 'declination', 'retrograde' (a filter on equal retrograde flags).

max_distance.description: Optional: only matches whose score (degrees) is at most this.

min_separation_days.description: Minimum gap between two matches and between a match and the reference time, so one passage gives one match. Raise it (e.g. 3650) to skip the current cycle of slow planets.

perspective.description: Positions seen from the Earth, from the Sun, or both.

range.description: Candidate dates. Default (a reference with a time): the longest window the caps allow, up to 100 years in the chosen direction (50 on each side for 'both').

reference.description: The sky to match: 'now' (default; the current UTC hour or day, echoed in result.reference.date_utc), a UTC moment ('2026-10-29T00:00Z' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'), {datetime: ...}, your own values {values: {feature id: value}} (add 'datetime' to anchor direction and range at a time), or a local date-time and place {place: {datetime: local '1990-05-15T14:30', latitude, longitude, timezone?}}: the time zone comes from the coordinates or 'timezone'; a date alone means 12:00 local with a TIME_UNKNOWN warning. meta.reference_resolution gives the equivalent {values, datetime} request. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde'.

require_same_retrograde.description: Keep only dates whose retrograde flags equal the reference's.

resolution.description: Step of the candidate grid. At most 36,600 candidate dates per call, and at most 660,000 dates x ephemeris series (one per body and perspective, plus one per retrograde-flagged body).

weights.description: Optional {feature id: weight}, default 1 each, e.g. {'geo.jupiter': 2}. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

name: similar_skies

accepts.description: x402 offer only: the payment options (scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo, ...).

endpoint.description: The REST route that computed it, e.g. 'astronomy/rise-set'.

error.description: x402 offer only: why payment is required.

deterministic.description: Always true: same input, same result.

llm_used.description: Always false: no language model is involved.

payment.description: How this call was paid: protocol ('free' or 'none'), price and the free calls remaining.

reproducibility.description: How to reproduce and check this result.

result_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical 'result'; check it with verify_result_hash.

resource.description: x402 offer only: the resource being paid for.

counts.description: Number of candidate dates, eligible dates and matches.

matches.description: Matching dates ranked by score: 'columns' format = {rank: [...], date_utc: [...], timestamp: [...], score: [...], <body or feature>: [...], distance:<feature id>: [...]}; 'rows' format = one object per match.

reference.description: The reference sky: its date_utc and timestamp with every body's longitude and retrograde flag (and matched angles / declinations), or the values you gave.

settings.description: Settings applied: reference source, direction, range, resolution, perspectives, bodies, features and their ids, weights, top_n, max_distance, min_separation_days, frames, column names and the metric definition (formula per feature).

title: Sky similarity search (matching skies)
